subject.title: fix(memory): exclude extraPaths from shared scope hash to avoid unnecessary reindexing

question: Should same-workspace agents share a builtin SQLite memory store by default, and if so what migration, session ownership, filtering, and SDK contract must ship with it?
rationale: The PR changes persistent memory storage and session visibility boundaries, and source inspection shows the current session sync model is agent-scoped rather than shared-store safe.

options.title: Redesign before merge
options.body: Require agent ownership/filtering, migration or rebuild-warning behavior, removal or acceptance of SDK exports, and latest-head proof before landing the shared store.

options.title: Accept directory as the boundary
options.body: Maintainers can intentionally choose same-workspace sharing, but the PR must document and prove the resulting migration and session-visibility semantics before merge.

options.title: Pause this branch
options.body: Keep the canonical issue open for design and avoid landing this incomplete storage-boundary implementation.

recommendation.title: Redesign before merge
recommendation.body: Require agent ownership/filtering, migration or rebuild-warning behavior, removal or acceptance of SDK exports, and latest-head proof before landing the shared store.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc has the strongest recent current-main history on the affected memory storage resolver and release-era memory behavior.
